record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Do analogous positive-density Lieb-Thirring inequalities exist for exponents γ<1, especially for γ=0 where the question is tied to bounds on spectral shift functions?

evidence.quote: Are there similar inequalities for γ < 1? In particular, for γ = 0 this is related to bounds for the spectral shift functions; see, e.g., [178, 158].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For $\gamma\ge 0$ and a real-valued potential $V$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, the classical Lieb–Thirring inequality asserts that the negative eigenvalues $\{-E_j(V)\}$ of the Schrödinger operator $-\Delta+V$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ satisfy
$$\sum_j E_j(V)^{\gamma}\;\le\; L_{\gamma,d}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma+d/2}\,dx,$$
where $V_-=\max(-V,0)$, and the inequality holds for $\gamma\ge 1/2$ if $d=1$, $\gamma>0$ if $d=2$, and $\gamma\ge 0$ if $d\ge 3$.

Positive-density setting. Let $\Pi_F$ denote the spectral projector of $-\Delta$ onto the Fermi sea $\{-\Delta\le \mu\}$ at chemical potential $\mu>0$, and consider the perturbed operator $-\Delta+V$. The positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequality (proved for $\gamma\ge 1$) bounds a quantity of the form
$$\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[(-\Delta+V-\mu)_-^{\gamma} - (-\Delta-\mu)_-^{\gamma}\right]$$
by an integral involving an appropriate power of $V_-$ (with constants depending on $\gamma$, $d$, and $\mu$).

Problem. Determine whether analogous positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequalities hold in the regime $\gamma<1$. In particular:

(a) For $0<\gamma<1$, does there exist a constant $C=C(\gamma,d,\mu)$ such that
$$\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[(-\Delta+V-\mu)_-^{\gamma} - (-\Delta-\mu)_-^{\gamma}\right] \;\le\; C\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma+d/2}\,dx$$
(or an appropriate variant involving both $V_-$ and $V_+$) for all sufficiently regular $V$?

(b) For $\gamma=0$, formulate and prove the corresponding bound, which is equivalent (in suitable formulations) to an $L^p$-type bound on the spectral shift function $\xi(\lambda;-\Delta+V,-\Delta)$ at energy $\lambda=\mu>0$ in terms of $\|V_-\|_{L^{d/2}}^{d/2}$ (or a comparable norm of $V$).
artifact.status_search_result: The positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequality was established by Frank–Lewin–Lieb–Seiringer (Duke Math. J., 2013) for exponents $\gamma\ge 1$. The extension to $\gamma<1$, and in particular the case $\gamma=0$ tied to $L^p$-bounds on the spectral shift function, is highlighted as an open question in the survey on recent results and open problems concerning Lieb–Thirring inequalities, and no general resolution appears in the subsequent literature retrieved (only partial results in special situations such as $\kappa=0$ in $d\ge 3$).

status_evidence.title: A positive density analogue of the Lieb-Thirring inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Frank, Lewin, Lieb, Seiringer establish positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequalities for the kinetic energy and for moments with γ≥1.
status_evidence.claim: The positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequality is known for γ≥1.

status_evidence.title: Lieb–Thirring inequality — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of known cases and open problems for Lieb–Thirring inequalities, including discussion of the case γ=0 and connections to spectral shift functions.
status_evidence.claim: The case γ<1 of positive-density Lieb–Thirring inequalities, including γ=0 and bounds on the spectral shift function, remains an open problem.
